answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring spatial signal transit to a specific vertex within a guarded grid. An issuer assigns geographic coordinates, and each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs; any latency drift exceeding a glacier-paced noise threshold triggers a penalty. Honest nodes pay linear travel costs, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion.
